axis: re-anchor local oracle onto a multi-dataset GT holdout (44b6x2 + 6bba x2) with per-dataset breakdown
hypothesis: The 2-family 44b6-only oracle drifted from the LB (DoG-v2 local 0.772 but LB 0.500). Scoring on all four test families (test *.zarr paired with train *.geff GT) will collapse DoG's inflated micro toward the LB and yield an LB-representative screen basis.
evidence: 4-family holdout micro-adj: v1_global_threshold=0.3598 (2-family 44b6=0.5063; LB 0.509), dog_v2=0.5225 (2-family 44b6=0.7721; LB 0.500). CONFIRMED: the expanded holdout collapses DoG's inflated 0.7721 -> 0.5225, ~LB 0.500, so the 2-family oracle was hiding DoG's 6bba degradation. NOT fully re-anchored: the holdout still ranks dog_v2 (0.5225) >> v1 (0.3598) whereas the LB ranks them ~tied with v1 marginally higher (0.509 vs 0.500), and v1's holdout micro (0.36) does not reproduce its own LB (0.509). Complementary per-dataset failure: v1 under-detects the dense 6bba_05db0fb1 (101/26/1082, adj 0.091), DoG over-detects the sparse 6bba_05b6850b (pred 40450 vs n_true 6362, adj 0.262). The 4-family holdout strictly supersedes the 2-family oracle as the screen basis but is not yet a faithful LB proxy for champion ranking; residual GT/normalization gap handed to SOT-2306 (re-judge champion) and SOT-2307 (adaptive intensity normalization). No Kaggle submission. See docs/reanchored-oracle-evaluation.json and docs/ai/sot-2305-oracle-reanchoring.md.

axis: adaptive robust-intensity DoG threshold (median + k*1.4826*MAD per volume) replacing the fixed percentile-92 cutoff, to stop dataset-scale over-detection
hypothesis: DoG-v2 keeps a fixed percentile (fixed voxel FRACTION) of the local-contrast response, so on sparse families (6bba_05b6850b: ~6362 true cells) it over-detects (pred 40450) and the node-count penalty crushes adjusted Jaccard to 0.262. A robust per-volume z-score threshold (median + k*1.4826*MAD) tracks each dataset own noise floor and adapts the kept-peak COUNT to signal content, equalising sensitivity across datasets with different intensity scales.
evidence: On the SOT-2305 4-dataset LB holdout, swept mad_k in {2,3,4,5,6,8,10}; k in {2,3,4} all beat the champion (holdout micro-adj 0.6016/0.6232/0.5979 vs champion 0.5225), a plateau not a spike, peak at k=3. Independent re-score via the real run_pipeline confirms mad_k=3.0: holdout micro-adj 0.5225->0.6232 (+0.1007). 6bba_05b6850b adj 0.262->0.502 (pred nodes 40450->13376) with matched-edge TP/FP/FN unchanged at 619/251/226 (the whole gain is pruning ~27000 spurious isolated detections the penalty punished, an honest node-count relief); 44b6 prefix held 0.7721->0.7716; 6bba_05db0fb1 held 0.7141->0.7096. Per-dataset precision/recall stay balanced (44b6 prec 0.88-0.96 rec 0.75-0.94; 6bba prec 0.71-0.85 rec 0.73-0.81) - no dataset collapses. Promoted to detect-link-dog-v3-adaptive; exec-compat gate + 55 pytest pass; embedded/config synced. No Kaggle submission. See experiments/sot2307/{screen_adaptive,confirm_adaptive}.json and docs/ai/sot-2307-adaptive-normalization.md.

axis: re-decide detection champion on the re-anchored 4-dataset LB oracle: DoG family vs pre-DoG v1 global-intensity-threshold (revert to global-threshold if DoG degrades)
hypothesis: The public LB moved 0.509->0.500 when DoG-v2 replaced the v1 global-threshold detector, suggesting DoG over-detects on the 6bba half of the real test set. If the SOT-2305 re-anchored 4-dataset holdout confirms DoG losing to global-threshold, the champion should REVERT to the LB-better global-threshold (LB 0.509) setting.
evidence: 3-way A/B on the SOT-2305 4-family holdout (size-weighted adjusted edge Jaccard, node-count over-detection penalty): v3_adaptive=0.6232 > dog_v2=0.5225 >> v1_global_threshold=0.3598. The DoG family strictly DOMINATES global-threshold on the re-anchored oracle, so the revert-to-global-threshold hypothesis is REJECTED and the champion is MAINTAINED at detect-link-dog-v3-adaptive (the SOT-2307 adaptive-MAD variant that is exactly the 'intermediate DoG + FP-suppression' option this issue lists). v1 collapses because it under-detects the dense 6bba_05db0fb1 (adj 0.091) and the fragmented 44b6_0b24845f (adj 0.044); DoG+adaptive holds all four families balanced (44b6 0.7716, 6bba 0.6168). Caveat inherited from SOT-2305: the oracle is not yet a faithful LB proxy for the v1-vs-DoG ranking (v1 holdout ~0.36 does not reproduce its LB 0.509; v1/dog_v2 are near-tied on LB) - that residual GT/normalization gap cannot be closed without a Kaggle submission, which this issue forbids. Decision uses the best available oracle. champion/config.json unchanged (already v3-adaptive); embedded EMBEDDED_CHAMPION_CONFIG in sync; exec-compat + 55 pytest pass. No Kaggle submission. See experiments/sot2306/champion_redecide.json and docs/ai/sot-2306-champion-redecision.md.

axis: port classical levers from the public frontier lineage tracker notebook (public 0.913, GPU pretrained UNet+ILP) into the CPU numpy/scipy/zarr pipeline: (a) motion-aware constant-velocity linking, (b) short-track pruning / FILTER_SHORT_TRACKS
hypothesis: The reference notebook's 0.913 comes from a GPU pretrained UNet-transformer + ILP solver (torch/tracksdata/pyscipopt/ilpy, CUDA T4+, external model dataset) that cannot run under this repo's self-contained numpy/scipy/zarr, CPU, no-internet, no-weights submission kernel. Only its classical post-processing transfers. A detection that never links into a multi-frame track is almost always noise; pruning short weakly-connected fragments should relieve the node-count penalty AND free GT nodes so the <=7um matching attaches the persistent track instead of a transient decoy.
evidence: Two levers screened on the SOT-2305 4-dataset LB holdout with the DoG-v3 detector frozen. (a) motion-aware linking (q_hat=q+gain*(q-q_prev), gains {0.5,1.0} x gate {actual,pred}) = REJECTED: helps sparse 44b6 but hurts dense 6bba (edge-count-weighted micro dominated by 6bba), holdout micro-adj 0.6232->{0.6218,0.6207,0.6188,0.6018}, never improves (experiments/sot2369/screen_motion.json). (b) short-track pruning min_track_length sweep {1,2,3,4,5}: micro rises monotonically 0.6232/0.6430/0.6602/0.6649/0.6692; mtl=5 regresses the clean 44b6_0113de3b family (edge TP 47->45, adj 0.8895->0.8539) by pruning real short tracks, so mtl=4 is the robust no-per-dataset-regression cutoff. At mtl=4 every dataset improves (adj 44b6_0113de3b 0.8814->0.8895, 44b6_0b24845f 0.6658->0.6817, 6bba_05b6850b 0.5025->0.5700, 6bba_05db0fb1 0.7096->0.7310) and matched-edge counts genuinely improve on the dense family (6bba_05b6850b TP 619->651, FP 251->215, FN 226->194 - not just node-count relief), holdout micro-adj 0.6232->0.6649 (+0.0417). Confirmed independently through champion_params()->run_pipeline (which caught a plumbing bug: champion_params was dropping link.min_track_length; fixed). Promoted to detect-link-dog-v4-shorttrack; 55 pytest + exec-compat gate pass; EMBEDDED_CHAMPION_CONFIG == champion/config.json. See experiments/sot2369/{screen_motion,screen_shorttrack,confirm_shorttrack}.json and docs/ai/sot-2369-short-track-pruning.md.
